name: Earl Sweatshirt
label: Warner Records
lede: Earl Sweatshirt starts out as a sixteen-year-old MySpace rapper in Odd Future, disappears to Samoa, comes back, and spends a decade making records that get quieter, stranger and better. The latest, a fatherhood album, is Pitchfork's No. 15 of 2025.

eras.title: Tyler finds a kid on MySpace
eras.text: A Los Angeles teenager raps under a joke name. Tyler, the Creator is building a crew that answers to no one, and finds him with a message.

years.h: Sly Tendencies posts raps on MySpace
years.p: Thebe Kgositsile is born in Chicago in 1994 and raised in Los Angeles by his mother, UCLA law professor Cheryl Harris. He starts rapping in seventh grade.
years.xp: Wikipedia says he also ran a rap trio, the Backpackerz, with friends Loofy and JW Mijo, which split in 2009. His father was the South African poet Keorapetse Kgositsile; his parents separated when he was six.

years.h: [[Odd Future|519336c2-f5a3-4137-a88e-58fecc604575]]'s first tape arrives three years before anyone cares
years.p: The Odd Future Tape comes out on November 15, self-released by [[Tyler, the Creator|f6beac20-5dfe-4d1f-ae02-0b0a740aafd6]], [[Hodgy|76600f02-c090-4d15-8782-680cde16bd98]], [[Left Brain|f57d8a69-ed3c-4d18-8bce-0083b162fae6]], [[Casey Veggies|67c6a1f0-7910-4c52-a651-2b7ec819e647]], [[Matt Martians|1018344f-abc8-4c62-b4fd-37a30fd2dc6f]] and [[Syd|7d3d6c65-e053-4657-8705-0ca61bc012ad]], a Los Angeles crew formed in 2007.
years.xp: The crew signed with RED Distribution and Sony in April 2011. Its first studio album, The OF Tape Vol. 2, arrived in March 2012, with Earl finally on it.

years.h: A MySpace message from Tyler turns Thebe into Earl Sweatshirt
years.p: Tyler finds the teenager on MySpace and brings him into Odd Future. The new name comes from its old-man sound and a James Pants sweatshirt.

eras.title: A mixtape at sixteen, then Samoa
eras.text: The most talked-about teenage rapper in America drops a mixtape and vanishes. Fans chant for him at shows while he sits in a boarding school on the other side of the Pacific.

years.h: Earl goes up free on the Odd Future site
years.p: Tyler produces most of it, with Vince Staples, Hodgy and Syd guesting. Pitchfork called it "mesmerizing" and later ranked it among the decade's 100 best albums.
years.xp: Recorded in 2009 and 2010 when Earl was 15 and 16, it was posted as a free download on the Odd Future website. Its graphic, violent narratives were fiction rather than autobiography, per Wikipedia, and reviewers argued over how vile verses could sound so fluent.

years.src: Wikipedia: Earl Sweatshirt · REVOLT: How Earl Sweatshirt grew up
years.h: Cheryl Harris sends him to Coral Reef Academy in Samoa
years.p: The school treats at-risk boys, and Earl stays about 18 months while "Free Earl" chants follow Odd Future from stage to stage.
years.xp:
Wikipedia reports that behavioral issues and drug use were cited as the reason. At the school he read Manning Marable's Malcolm X biography, and he wrote verses that later ended up on the Odd Future track "Oldie."

REVOLT describes the stay as a turning point: he talked with abuse survivors and worked through his complicated feelings about his father.

years.h: Complex finds Earl in Samoa, then The New Yorker hears from him
years.p: Complex confirms in April that he is at Coral Reef Academy. In May Kelefa Sanneh publishes emails in The New Yorker in which Earl says he is not held against his will.
years.xp:
Tyler Craven, an alumnus of the school who had helped Complex find Earl, disputed that account in June, saying on Facebook that the quotes were shaped by staff therapists.

The New Yorker piece also has him asking fans to stop the Free Earl chants. Nobody stopped.

years.h: Tupac's old manager brings him home
years.p: Leila Steinberg, who once managed Tupac Shakur, gets Earl back from Samoa in February 2012. Wikipedia lists her as still his manager.

years.h: Earl joins Odd Future at Hammerstein Ballroom the night Vol. 2 drops
years.p: The OF Tape Vol. 2, released March 20, is his first album with the crew, and he appears on "Oldie."

years.h: Columbia signs him, and he turns down bigger offers
years.p: He gets his own imprint, Tan Cressida, and passes on larger money to stay close to Odd Future.

years.h: Earl raps on [[Frank Ocean|e520459c-dff4-491d-a6e4-c97be35e0044]]'s Channel Orange
years.p: "Super Rich Kids" puts him on Ocean's debut album, and Wikipedia notes he was nominated for Album of the Year as a featured artist.

years.src: Wikipedia: Chum (song) · IMVDb: Hiro Murai on Chum
years.h: Earl comes back with "Chum," vocals cut in one take
years.p: It's his first solo single since Samoa, recorded in the first three days of album sessions with [[Christian Rich|e5b5b041-bf22-4658-b58a-8be875674a4c]]. Pitchfork named it Best New Track.
years.xp:
Director Hiro Murai hung Earl upside down for the performance shots and added the frogs in post. Tyler and his crew turned up mid-shoot riding shopping carts and stormed the set, Murai told IMVDb.

Pitchfork's Larry Fitzmaurice wrote that it was "someone growing into their lyrical talents as they grow up in real time." Wikipedia says it has since gone Gold in the US.

eras.title: Doris and the late-night circuit
eras.text: The debut album arrives with a Billboard top five, a late-night TV spot and a sketch-comedy job. Earl spends it telling everyone he hates the attention.

years.cap: Tyler and Earl at the Fox Theater, Pomona, May 25, 2013
years.src: Stereogum: Tyler, Earl Sweatshirt and Domo Genesis play Letterman
yt: Tyler, Earl and Domo Genesis on Letterman
years.h: Odd Future does "Rusty" on Letterman, then poses with the host
years.p: Tyler, Earl and [[Domo Genesis|0ad99596-cbec-4726-af16-138e2a9268a1]] hang at the back of the stage during Tyler's "Rusty," stalk off, and return to snap a picture with David Letterman.

years.h: Doris is the album about not wanting to be famous
years.p: Recorded from February 2012 to July 2013, with beats from Earl (as randomblackdude), the Neptunes, [[RZA|29c28ac3-27c5-4822-8eb6-0af89a3a7240]] and Christian Rich; debuts at No. 5 on the Billboard 200.
years.xp: Guests include [[Frank Ocean|e520459c-dff4-491d-a6e4-c97be35e0044]], [[Vince Staples|78e854b8-9713-4ff2-9218-6b3784893bff]], [[Mac Miller|a0e8a1b1-5f8f-475a-a253-17415c17d0ff]] and Tyler. The Guardian and the Los Angeles Times gave it top marks, per Wikipedia, and Complex ranked it No. 11 on its 2013 albums list.

years.cap: Earl at the Fox Theater, Pomona, May 25, 2013
years.h: Earl spends twenty episodes on Loiter Squad
years.p: The Adult Swim sketch show Odd Future fronts runs from 2012 to 2014, and Earl is a regular. He also plays "Burgundy" with the Roots on Late Night with Jimmy Fallon.

eras.title: Less, on purpose
eras.text: Earl sheds the crew, the label's plan and most of the beats. He puts out an album with no warning and a ten-minute EP on a nameless YouTube account.

years.cap: Earl at the SPIN party, SXSW, Austin, March 20, 2015
years.src: Wikipedia: I Don't Like Shit, I Don't Go Outside · Wikipedia: Earl Sweatshirt
years.h: A 30-minute album turns up on iTunes with no announcement
years.p: Earl says the label put out I Don't Like Shit, I Don't Go Outside without notice. He calls it his first real album because he can "back up everything, the good and the bad."
years.xp:
The only Odd Future guest is Vince Staples, alongside Dash, Wiki and Na-Kel Smith. It debuted at No. 12 on the Billboard 200 and Pitchfork ranked it 25th among 2015's albums, per Wikipedia.

Sources differ on the date: the album's Wikipedia page says pre-orders appeared March 17 and it came out March 23, while his artist page says March 16 and March 22.
play: I Don't Like Shit, I Don't Go Outside

years.h: Earl uploads "Solace" for his mother and grandmother
years.p: That is Earl's own description of the ten-minute EP, which goes up on a YouTube channel called dar Qness.

years.big: "Thebe and I are fine by the way." Tyler
years.src: DIY: Earl Sweatshirt and Tyler, the Creator comment on Odd Future being over · Wikipedia: Odd Future
years.h: Tyler says Odd Future is over. Then he says it isn't
years.p: He tweets that although it's no more, "those 7 letters are forever." Earl tweets that he is out.
years.xp: Tyler said he had only been looking at old photos and thinking about how time flies, and that one tweet had stirred everything up. The group stayed mostly dormant after 2015, per Wikipedia, and reunited for shows in 2018 and 2023.

years.h: Earl drops three tracks on SoundCloud in one day
years.p: "Wind in My Sails" (with an Alchemist beat), "Bary" and "Skrt Skrt" appear on January 25.

eras.title: The shortest, most private record
eras.text: Earl moves toward the New York underground and makes a 25-minute album. His father has died, and the samples on it belong to both parents.

years.cap: Earl at Day N Night Festival, August 12, 2017
years.src: DJBooth: Earl Sweatshirt's Some Rap Songs one year later
years.h: Earl falls in with MIKE and the sLUms crew in New York
years.p: He gets to know MIKE, Medhane and others from the sLUms scene at XL Recordings, and is in their orbit by 2018.
years.xp: The album sessions started in a home studio in Los Angeles in December 2016 and ran through 2018, per Wikipedia. Producers included Adé Hakim, Black Noi$e, Denmark Vessey and [[Navy Blue|304c731f-ea4f-407c-b4fc-65131b1b2b37]] (Sage Elsesser).

years.src: Wikipedia: Earl Sweatshirt · NPR: Earl Sweatshirt interview transcript
years.h: Earl's father, the poet Keorapetse Kgositsile, dies
years.p: He lived far from Earl's California childhood, and Wikipedia calls the relationship complex and often distant.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the death to January 2018, citing Pitchfork. Earl said the coming album was meant to be themed around his father's death. On NPR he spoke of the frustration of losing his "pops."

years.h: Earl tweets "tap in" and "Nowhere2go" lands the next morning
years.p: [[Vince Staples|78e854b8-9713-4ff2-9218-6b3784893bff]] had announced a new Earl album on Beats 1 on November 2. Earl's tweet comes on November 7.

years.src: Wikipedia: Some Rap Songs · DJBooth: Earl Sweatshirt's Some Rap Songs one year later
years.h: Some Rap Songs fits 15 tracks into 25 minutes
years.p: Lo-fi and sample-heavy, it closes with "Playing Possum," built on vocal samples of his late father and his mother. It debuts at No. 17 on the Billboard 200.
years.xp:
The album opens on a James Baldwin sample about imprecise words, and Navy Blue and Standing on the Corner both appear. Metacritic gave it an 86 from 19 reviews, per Wikipedia.

Earl told NPR the title was literal: "swear to God that's some rap songs right there."

years.h: The Columbia deal ends with Some Rap Songs
years.p: Earl tells fans the record is his last for Columbia and that he is excited to be free.

years.h: Feet of Clay arrives with one day's notice
years.p: Warner Records releases the 15-minute EP with beats from The Alchemist, Black Noi$e and Mach-Hommy. A deluxe edition with two bonus tracks follows in July 2020.

eras.title: Out from under Columbia
eras.text: Now on Warner and pushing further into rough sound, Earl releases a pandemic-era album, then a full album with the Alchemist that arrives through a very online door.

years.h: Two years of quiet end with "2010"
years.p: Earl returns with the single and video for "2010." In December "Tabula Rasa," featuring Armand Hammer, announces his fourth album.

years.h: Sick! peaks at No. 5 on the Billboard 200
years.p: Ten songs, an 85 on Metacritic, and guests including Armand Hammer and Zelooperz.
years.xp:
Earl called it his "humble offering of 10 songs recorded in the wake of the worldwide coronavirus pandemic." Production came from Earl, The Alchemist, Black Noi$e, Navy Blue, Samiyam, Theravada and others.

Stereogum's Tom Breihan made it Album of the Week.

years.src: Wikipedia: Voir Dire (Earl Sweatshirt and the Alchemist album)
years.h: The Alchemist album comes as a website puzzle and an NFT
years.p: Voir Dire, made entirely with [[The Alchemist|03f3deb7-0419-4bf9-a1e7-511946385717]], is announced through a puzzle and released via Gala Music. The NFT tie-in draws backlash.
years.xp: Recorded from late 2020 to 2021, it ended up on streaming services on October 6 with a slightly different tracklist that adds Vince Staples features. Metacritic gave it 83 from nine reviews, per Wikipedia.

eras.title: Live Laugh Love
eras.text: A father and married man makes his shortest, weirdest and most tender record, and the year-end critics notice.

years.src: Wikipedia: Live Laugh Love (Earl Sweatshirt album)
years.h: An impostor plays Earl's album launch
years.p: The Los Angeles listening event announces the album with Earl absent. An Earl Sweatshirt impersonator performs, and Black Noi$e DJs from the record.

q: I guess the joke was on me.
years.src: Wikipedia: Live Laugh Love · Metacritic: Live Laugh Love critic reviews · Year-End Lists: Pitchfork
years.h: Pitchfork gives Live Laugh Love an 8.5 and ranks it No. 15 of 2025
years.p: The 24-minute, 11-track album (Tan Cressida/Warner) is built from Theravada, Black Noi$e, Child Actor and Navy Blue production, and scores an 84 on Metacritic.
years.xp:
Earl told the New York Times Popcast that the title holds both halves of him: "being 16 and then also having a family." Pitchfork's review is listed at 85 on Metacritic, which quotes it: "There's so much musical and personal inspiration colliding at once, you can feel the passion even when you can't quite crack it all."

It peaked at No. 184 on the Billboard 200. Videos followed for "Crisco", "Exhaust" and "Well Done!"

eras.title: Utility
eras.text: The next move is a shared double album with the New York rapper he learned from.

years.cap: Earl Sweatshirt and MIKE at VIVID Live, Sydney Opera House, May 2026
years.h: Earl and MIKE share a double album, all produced by Surf Gang
years.p: MIKE's Pompeii and Earl's 18-track Utility sit on one release, with sessions in New York and Los Angeles between 2023 and 2025.
years.xp: Pitchfork gave it 7.3, per Wikipedia. Utility runs 35 minutes, and MIKE appears on "Leadbelly."
